---
title: "B then D"
subtitle: "On-policy distillation on top of B"
---

{{< include /_setup.qmd >}}

**Question.** Thinking Machines start on-policy distillation from a fine-tuned checkpoint. Does D's
loss improve B, rather than replace it?

**Setup.** B's selected checkpoint, continued with D's loss at a quarter of D's learning rate,
stopped early, with checkpoints every 100 steps to see whether it gains fast. Reported as a pipeline,
not as method D.

::: {.facts}
```{python}
table(["B→D", "B"])
```
:::

```{ojs}
runs = ["B→D"]
```

{{< include /_run.qmd >}}

## What it shows

- **It doesn't help.** No checkpoint beat B on validation. The selected one is behind B on
  test-clean under strict exact (`{python} story.claim("B→D", "B", "test-clean")`), and level under
  lenient: it moves B toward the teacher's conventions about defaults.
- **On unseen tools it is level with B and below D**
  (`{python} story.claim("B→D", "D", "bfcl")`). One learning rate and one seed; the run wasn't
  resumed.

::: {.column-margin}
The run: [#58](https://github.com/joaomigueloliveira/qwen-function-calling-distillation/issues/58);
why it is a pipeline: [ADR 0008](../decisions/0008-method-d-setup.html); training curves:
`{python} wandb("B→D")`.
:::
